modules.title: Dataverse and platform governance
modules.summary: Explains Dataverse modeling and platform governance concepts.

lessons.title: Microsoft Dataverse foundations
lessons.summary: Learn how Dataverse stores business data with tables, columns, relationships, forms, views, business rules, security, Power Fx, and AI-assisted modeling.
learningObjectives: Describe Dataverse tables, columns, rows, and relationships
Identify forms, views, and business rules used in model-driven data experiences
Explain how security roles control access to Dataverse data
Recognize how Power Fx and AI-assisted modeling support app makers
lessons.explanation: Dataverse is the secure business data platform for Power Platform. Tables contain rows and typed columns; relationships connect tables; forms and views shape how users work; and business rules or Power Fx add logic. Compared with a traditional database, Dataverse also provides rich metadata, standard tables, role-based security, Dynamics 365 integration, and maker-friendly tools. AI can help create or edit tables, columns, and relationships, but the data model still needs review. Practise this in the Create a Dataverse table and a canvas app lab.

terminology.definition: A typed value on a row.

lessons.businessScenario: Contoso Facilities has one spreadsheet for departments, requesters, technicians, and repair tasks. Priya wants to turn those repeated columns into related Dataverse tables so dispatchers stop copying the same department details into every row.
lessons.technicalExample: Model `Department` with Name and Cost Center, `Equipment Request` with Status, Priority, Requester, and a lookup to Department, and `Request Task` with Due Date and a lookup to Equipment Request. Add an Open Requests view and a business rule that requires Justification when Priority is High.

misconception.myth: Dataverse tables are just spreadsheet tabs with a new name.
misconception.reality: Dataverse tables include typed columns, relationships, forms, views, business rules, auditing and role-based access that spreadsheets do not provide by themselves.

lessons.examTakeaway: When a scenario mentions rows, columns, relationships, forms, views, Dynamics 365 data, or reusable validation logic, think Dataverse before thinking about a standalone file.
lessons.recap: Learn how Dataverse stores business data with tables, columns, relationships, forms, views, business rules, security, Power Fx, and AI-assisted modeling.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Dataverse is more like a city records office than a spreadsheet: each form has approved fields, related records point to each other, and clerks only see the files their badge allows.
lessons.anotherExample: A volunteer charity could model Volunteers, Events, and Assignments as related Dataverse tables, then let coordinators filter a view to this weekend’s unfilled shifts.

data.title: Normalize the request sheet
data.instructions: Decide whether each spreadsheet column should become a table, column, or relationship in Dataverse.

items.prompt: Department name appears on every equipment request row.
items.answer: Create a Department table and relate Equipment Request rows to it.

items.prompt: Priority contains High, Normal, or Low.
items.answer: Use a choice column on Equipment Request.

items.prompt: Several repair tasks belong to one request.
items.answer: Create a Request Task table related to Equipment Request.

flashcards.back: A row represents one business item, such as one equipment request, with typed columns describing it.
A column that connects a row in one table to a row in another table, such as a request to a department.
A business rule can apply validation or defaulting logic to Dataverse data without writing plug-ins.
Forms edit one row; views list many rows filtered or sorted for a task.

lessons.title: Administer and govern Power Platform environments
lessons.summary: Learn how environments, admin center, data policies, security roles, managed environments, monitoring, privacy, accessibility, and ALM fit together.
learningObjectives: Describe how environments separate Power Platform apps, flows, and data
Identify admin center tools for monitoring, security, and data policies
Explain how managed environments and ALM support governed delivery
Choose governance actions for privacy, accessibility, and lifecycle needs
lessons.explanation: Governance makes the easy path the safe path. Environments separate apps, flows, data, agents, and audiences. The Power Platform admin center manages environments, security, Copilot governance, monitoring, deployments, licensing, and support. Data policies govern connector use. Security roles define what users can create, open, or edit. Managed environments add scale controls such as sharing limits, usage insights, pipelines, and solution checker. Privacy, accessibility, monitoring, and ALM all matter. Practise this in the governed environment and data policy lab.

terminology.definition: A container for apps, flows, data, agents, and connections.
Connector governance that reduces data exposure risk.
Premium capabilities for administration at scale.

lessons.businessScenario: Fabrikam’s facilities app is ready for a pilot, but legal requires connector guardrails, IT wants a separate sandbox, and operations wants only approved makers touching production.
lessons.technicalExample: Create a Sandbox environment named Facilities Dev, restrict maker access to the Facilities Makers security group, enable Dataverse, apply a data policy that keeps Dataverse and Outlook in the business connector group, and promote the solution to production through a pipeline.

misconception.myth: A Power Platform administrator role is the same thing as permission to read every Dataverse row.
misconception.reality: Tenant and environment admin roles manage platform settings, while Dataverse security roles still control data privileges inside each environment.

lessons.examTakeaway: For administration questions, separate the container (environment), the people permissions (environment and Dataverse roles), connector guardrails (data policies), and release path (solutions and pipelines).
lessons.recap: Learn how environments, admin center, data policies, security roles, managed environments, monitoring, privacy, accessibility, and ALM fit together.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Governance is like running a makerspace: people get badges for specific rooms, some tools cannot be combined, and finished projects leave through a supervised checkout desk.
lessons.anotherExample: A retailer can let store managers prototype in a sandbox while production apps are locked to approved security groups and monitored through managed environment insights.

data.title: Administer and govern Power Platform environments
data.caption: Business data is modeled, protected with roles and policies, then used by apps.

data.title: Choose the governance control
data.instructions: Match the admin concern to the control you would discuss first.

items.prompt: Makers should not mix payroll data with consumer social connectors.
items.answer: Create or update a data policy.

items.prompt: Only the HR app team should build in a new environment.
items.answer: Restrict environment access and assign maker roles to the group.

items.prompt: A tested solution must move from test to production.
items.answer: Use managed solutions and Power Platform pipelines.

flashcards.back: An environment separates resources such as apps, flows, connections, agents, and Dataverse data for a purpose or audience.
Data policies classify or block connectors to reduce unintended data movement.
Managed environments add admin-at-scale capabilities such as sharing limits, insights, pipelines, and solution checker.
A tenant admin can manage platform settings but still needs Dataverse roles for data privileges.

options.text: Every maker automatically has all Dataverse access.

knowledgeCheck.stem: A tenant-level admin role automatically grants every Dataverse table privilege in every environment.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Tenant administration and Dataverse table privileges are different permission layers, so the statement is false.

options.explanation: Choosing True confuses tenant administration with Dataverse data permissions; table privileges are granted through environment-scoped Dataverse security roles.
Correct. A tenant-level admin role does not automatically grant every Dataverse table privilege, because Dataverse uses separate security roles.

knowledgeCheck.stem: Order the dependent steps for applying connector governance to a new maker environment before users begin building.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The environment must exist before it can be scoped by a data policy; connector groups are configured in that policy before makers are granted access.

items.text: Create or select the target environment
Add that environment as the scope of a data policy
Classify required connectors in the policy and save it
Assign maker roles after the scoped policy is active

explanations.s1: The environment is the governance boundary that later policy and role steps target.
explanations.s2: A data policy can be scoped to the environment only after that environment exists.
explanations.s3: Connector classifications must be saved in the scoped policy before it can govern maker activity.
explanations.s4: Makers should receive roles after the policy is active so their work starts under the intended connector rules.
